verifications.claim: NASA officially targets early 2028 for the Artemis IV crewed lunar landing mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis IV (early 2028) is planned to be the first American crewed lunar landing'; 'As of March 2026, NASA is targeting early 2028 for launch.' R4: 'As of March 2026, NASA is targeting early 2028 for launch.' R1: 'Artemis 4 moon landing... slated to launch in 2028.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state NASA targets early 2028 for Artemis IV lunar landing launch.

verifications.claim: Some estimates cite September 2028 for the Artemis IV crewed lunar landing mission.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Current public announcements call for launching no earlier than September 2028'
verifications.reasoning: R6 mentions September 2028 as a public announcement target, supporting 'some estimates' but not precisely matching phrasing or specifying 'estimates'.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV will utilize the Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1B rocket.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA previously planned to upgrade SLS... to a Block 1B... but cancelled these plans in February 2026, aiming to standardize on Block 1.' R4: 'potentially... Centaur V upper stage... Artemis IV may instead use the ICPS'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS for Artemis IV but explicitly state Block 1B upgrade was cancelled; will use Block 1 or standardized config.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV will deliver the International Habitation Module (I-Hab) to the Lunar Gateway.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Before October 2022, the goal for Artemis IV was simply to deliver the I-HAB module... before the Lunar Gateway was cancelled in February 2026.' R4: 'Before October 2022, the goal for Artemis IV was simply to deliver the I-HAB module... before the Lunar Gateway was cancelled.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state this was a past plan, changed after Gateway cancellation; now first lunar landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV will transport astronauts to the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis IV... first crewed lunar landing... astronauts will transfer to the lander for descent to the lunar surface.' R4: 'two astronauts will transfer to it, descend to the lunar surface.' R3: 'Artemis 4 will now be the first lunar landing mission.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm Artemis IV includes crewed lunar landing/surface transport.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is the second crewed lunar landing of the program after Artemis III.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III (mid-2027)... test HLS lunar lander in Earth orbit.' 'Artemis IV (early 2028)... first... crewed lunar landing.' R3: 'Artemis 4 will now be the first lunar landing.' R4: 'first lunar landing of the NASA-led Artemis program.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state Artemis III is Earth orbit tests (no landing); Artemis IV is the first crewed lunar landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV's location is the Lunar South Pole.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the extreme southerly latitude of the Artemis 4 landing sites... south polar region.' R2: 'Most landing sites are near the lunar south pole... to support the Artemis lunar program.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify Artemis IV landing sites at lunar south pole/southerly latitudes.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is targeted for early 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026).' R3: 'Artemis 2 launched on 1 April 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm April 1, 2026 target/launch, which is early 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is targeted for mid-2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III (mid-2027).' R3: 'targeted launch in mid-2027.' R5: 'Artemis III, in 2027.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state mid-2027 target for Artemis III.

verifications.claim: The Artemis IV timeline remains subject to the success and scheduling of the preceding Artemis II and Artemis III missions.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The Artemis program is organized around a series of missions of increasing complexity... Missions after Artemis II will also rely on support missions.' R4: 'The mission depends on a prior support flight.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe sequential program structure where later missions depend on prior successes, implying Artemis IV timeline is subject to Artemis II/III.
